clue.text: Those bearing heavy loads for old physician?

definitions.text: Those bearing heavy loads for old physician?

parts.words: Those bearing heavy loads for old physician?
parts.note: read as two words, boxes that carry river horses would bear heavy loads; read whole, it is the father of medicine

explanation.surface: A riddle about porters or carriers working for an elderly doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as HIPPO CRATES: crates holding hippos certainly bear heavy loads. Whole, it is the ancient Greek doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippocrates was the ancient Greek doctor credited as the founder of Western medicine.

clue.text: Impenetrable second book

parts.note: hard means difficult to get through or understand
to second a motion is to back or support it

explanation.surface: A dense, difficult second volume in a series.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardback is a volume bound in stiff covers, as opposed to a paperback.

clue.text: Leg across a surprisingly long, scaly animal

indicators.note: the leg word lies across, that is spans around, the mixed letters

parts.note: pins is slang for legs, so a leg is a pin

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that a long appears in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A long leg stretching across a strangely lengthy scaly creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The pangolin is an anteater-like mammal covered in overlapping protective scales.

clue.text: Greasy attention seeker came first

parts.note: oi is the shout used to get someone's attention
led means was in front, came first in a race

explanation.surface: A slick show-off who always pushed to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: Oi! is a British exclamation to attract someone's attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Something oiled has been coated with lubricant, so it is slippery and slick.

clue.text: Farmer managed chickens initially and cattle briefly?

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it, so managed gives ran

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of chickens
briefly says the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a herd is a group of cattle

explanation.surface: A farmer who ran a poultry business at first and cattle for a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: A rancher runs a large livestock farm, especially in North America.

clue.text: One overwhelmed by jobs, rants

indicators.note: to be overwhelmed is to be engulfed, so the one goes inside the jobs

parts.note: trades are jobs or occupations
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An overworked person vents furiously about the workload.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirades are long angry speeches, outbursts of denunciation.

clue.text: A half a trifle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a half pint, a small measure of beer in a British pub
second meaning: something unimportant, a matter of little consequence

explanation.walkthrough: In a British pub 'a half' is a half-pint glass of beer, a small beer; trifle looks like the pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Small beer literally was weak ale, and figuratively is anything petty or insignificant.

clue.text: TV or radio tune

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to adjust or regulate

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests tuning in a broadcast; the two halves are separate senses of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: A set is a receiver for broadcasts, and to set something is to adjust it to the right position.

clue.text: Pair swerving left after first of skiers go downhill fast

indicators.note: the left letter comes after the rest
picks the opening letter of skiers
swerving changes direction, so the letters of pair weave into a new order

explanation.surface: Two skiers swerving left behind the leader as they race downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go downhill fast' looks like skiing, but it means to decline rapidly.
explanation.definitionFit: To spiral is to worsen ever more quickly, as costs or a crisis can.

clue.text: Figure walked off in case of treachery

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other, the walking word inside the outer letters
a case surrounds its contents, so only the outer letters of treachery are used

parts.note: went means walked off, departed

explanation.surface: Someone walked out of a trial over a betrayal.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty is a number, and figure is a common word for any numeral.

clue.text: Learn to brew using filters?

indicators.note: brewing stirs ingredients together, so the letters of learn are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice on learning to make coffee or beer with filters.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the kidneys filter the blood, so anything relating to them works by filtering, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal means relating to the kidneys, the organs that filter waste out of the blood.

clue.text: Scandinavian touring country put things in usual manner

indicators.note: a tourist goes round a place, so the Scandinavian word goes around the country

parts.note: Norse means Scandinavian, especially of old Norway
Mali is a West African country

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian traveller on a foreign trip arranges everything just as at home.
explanation.definitionFit: To normalise is to bring something back to its standard or regular state.

clue.text: Passion dropped for butchery

parts.note: blood stands for passion or temper, as in hot blood or one's blood being up
shed means dropped, as leaves or skin are shed

explanation.surface: Someone's passion dropped away in favour of slaughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodshed is the killing or wounding of people, a synonym for slaughter.

clue.text: Lowest point on back of heel

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece placed on another follows it
the back of a word is its final letter, here the end of heel

parts.note: east is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Describes the lowest spot of a shoe, at the back of the heel.
explanation.definitionFit: Least means smallest in amount or degree, the bottom of a scale.

clue.text: Jolly carpenter, say

definitions.meaning: second meaning: one who chips wood, a joiner or carpenter, nicknamed a chippy; say marks an example

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a cheerful tradesman, but the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Chipper is informal for cheerful and bright, and literally one who chips, as a woodworker does.

clue.text: Reply sent off in the next hour or so?

definitions.text: in the next hour or so?

indicators.note: off means wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An email response will be sent within an hour or so.
explanation.definitionFit: Presently means soon, shortly, a little while from now.

clue.text: Stop contributing to funds, temporarily

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone halts their payments into a fund for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to check or halt it, as in stemming bleeding.

clue.text: Cooler dancing and vitality in dance

parts.note: a fan is a device that cools

indicators.note: dancing moves around, so the letters of and change places

parts.note: go means energy or vitality, as in full of go

explanation.surface: A calmer person dancing with energy at a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The fandango is a lively Spanish courtship dance in triple time.

clue.text: Wake–up call, on French city invaded by English

parts.note: re means on, concerning, as in business letters

indicators.note: an invaded place has someone inside it, so the English letter goes inside

parts.note: ville is French for city or town

explanation.surface: An alarm sounds in a French town as the English invade.
explanation.definitionFit: Reveille is the bugle signal sounded to rouse soldiers in the morning.

clue.text: Don Quixote's back put into crusade

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another, here the final letter going into the campaign word

parts.note: a crusade was a holy war

indicators.note: the back of Quixote is the last letter of his name

parts.note: the name Quixote, the possessive marking that the back is his

explanation.surface: Pictures Don Quixote, the deluded knight, being sent off on a crusade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like the title before Quixote's name, but it is the verb meaning to put on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To don clothing is to put it on, which is to wear it.

clue.text: Random article in account

indicators.note: random means haphazard, so the letters of article fall in no fixed order

explanation.surface: A chance newspaper piece appears in a report.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a detailed telling or narration of events.

clue.text: Deck, where boy cut card

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the boy's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Terry is a boy's name
an ace is a playing card

explanation.surface: Sets a scene on a ship's deck where a lad is cutting a pack of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' suggests a pack of cards beside 'card', but here it means a raised patio.
explanation.definitionFit: A deck is a raised outdoor platform by a house, much like a paved patio area.

clue.text: Deport foreign leader of opposition, wreck

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange or altered, so the letters of deport are rearranged
picks the opening letter of opposition

explanation.surface: A call to expel the foreign head of the opposition and ruin them.
explanation.definitionFit: To torpedo a plan is to sabotage or destroy it.

clue.text: Large cracks spoiled a rice cake

indicators.note: the large letter cracks into, breaking open, the mixed letters
spoiled means messed up, so the letters of a rice are rearranged

parts.note: L is the clothing size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A big crack ruins a batch of rice pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a finger-shaped choux pastry filled with cream and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: Shop cleared out, jewellery in vault

indicators.note: with its middle emptied, only the outer letters of shop remain

parts.note: a ring is an item of jewellery

explanation.surface: A shop emptied by thieves, with jewellery hidden in its strongroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vault' looks like a strongroom, but it is the verb for leaping.
explanation.definitionFit: To vault is to leap over something, and spring is a synonym for jump.

clue.text: Nails ending in some wood

parts.note: to nail a criminal is to catch them; to cop is also to catch, so nails gives cops

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, here the end of some

explanation.surface: A carpenter's nails with ends sunk into some timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nails' looks like hardware for wood, but it is the slang verb for catching someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small thicket of trees, a little stand of woodland.

clue.text: Case in bank put on trolley

indicators.note: in an across answer, a piece put on another comes after it

parts.note: a cart is a trolley, as in a shopping cart
a ridge is a raised bank of earth

explanation.surface: A security case at a bank is loaded onto a trolley.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartridge is a casing holding ammunition, ink or film.

clue.text: Puzzle book stolen by litigant turned up

indicators.note: in a down answer, turned up means read from bottom to top
what is stolen is taken in, so the book letter goes inside the litigant

parts.note: a suer is one who sues, a litigant

explanation.surface: A puzzle book stolen by someone suing has turned up again.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a picture riddle in which images and letters represent words.

clue.text: Noble head on the discontented Lebanese philosopher

parts.note: aristo is short for aristocrat, a noble

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of the
with its contents removed, only the outer letters of Lebanese remain

explanation.surface: A noble figure heads a group of unhappy Lebanese people.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the ancient Greek thinker, pupil of Plato.

clue.text: Refuse almost all stock

parts.note: to ban is to refuse or forbid

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so all loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Turning down nearly the whole of one's inventory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' looks like goods held, but here it is the adjective for something trite, as in a stock phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Banal means trite and unoriginal, like a stock response.

clue.text: Jazz magazine

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ragtime, an early syncopated jazz style
second meaning: a low-quality newspaper or magazine

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like the title of a music periodical; the two words are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag is a ragtime piece, and is also slang for a trashy periodical.

clue.text: National Park where chicken put to death

parts.note: chicken and yellow both mean cowardly
to stone someone is to execute them by throwing stones

explanation.surface: A grim scene in a reserve where a bird is killed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chicken' looks like the bird, but it is the adjective for cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellowstone in Wyoming was the first such protected area in the United States, famous for geysers.
